hints.title: Midpoint Disconnection Obstacle
hints.text: Unlike an indexed array, a linked list does not provide direct random access to the middle element. How can moving at different step rates locate the midpoint to partition the list into balanced halves?

hints.title: Slow-Fast Bisect Invariant
hints.text: Find the middle node using slow and fast pointers while disconnecting the left half from the midpoint. The middle becomes the root, recursing on left and right segments.

hints.title: Halving Sublist Recursion Procedure
hints.text: If head is null, return null. If head.next is null, return TreeNode(head.val). Use slow and fast pointers with a prev pointer to find the middle. Disconnect prev.next to terminate the left list. Create TreeNode(slow.val), recurse left on head, and recurse right on slow.next.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in list (0 <= N <= 2 * 10^4)
complexity.notes: Finding the midpoint takes O(N) per level across O(log N) recursive tree levels.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Converting the list to an array consumes O(N) auxiliary space instead of O(log N) stack frames.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(log N) stack depth with in-place pointer disconnection.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Severing the prev.next pointer to prevent cycles or infinite recursion.
